questions.question: How does "I am happy" change in reported speech?
options: She said she was happy.
She said she is happy now.
She said I am happy.
She said she will be happy.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, the tense moves one step back: present simple "am" becomes past simple "was", and the pronoun changes from I to she.

questions.question: What does "I will help" become in reported speech?
options: She said she would help.
She said she will helped.
She said she can help.
She said she had help.
questions.explanation: "Will" changes to "would" in reported speech: "I will help" → "She said she would help."

questions.question: What does the time expression "tomorrow" usually become in reported speech?
options: the next day / the following day
yesterday
that day
last week
questions.explanation: Time expressions shift in reported speech: tomorrow → the next day, yesterday → the day before, today → that day, now → then.

questions.question: How do you report the question "Where do you live?"
options: She asked me where I lived.
She asked me where did I live.
She asked me where do you live.
She asked me where I live?
questions.explanation: Reported questions use statement word order (no do/did) and back-shifted tense: "She asked me where I lived."

questions.question: How do you report the command "Open the window!"?
options: She told me to open the window.
She told me open the window.
She said me to open the window.
She told that I open the window.
questions.explanation: Reported commands use told + object + to + infinitive: "She told me to open the window."
